1.title: Get Data: Sources, Storage Modes and Parameters
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Get Data: Sources, Storage Modes and Parameters. It covers the exam area Prepare the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Identify and connect to data sources or a shared semantic model. Change data source settings, including credentials and privacy levels. Choose between Direct Lake, Direct Query, and Import. Create and modify parameters. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Prepare the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models
1.text: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models. On the Home tab of Power B I Desktop, Get data opens the list of Power Query connectors: files such as Excel, C S V, Jason and X M L, databases, online services, cloud sources and the web. Pick a connector, sign in, then choose Load or Transform Data.

1.title: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models, continued
1.text: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models. The figure shows this: Import copies data into the model, Direct Query asks the source for every visual, and Direct Lake reads Delta tables in One Lake without copying them.

1.title: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models, continued
1.text: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models. Load. The data goes straight into the model. Transform Data. The Power Query Editor opens so you can clean and shape first. Some connectors also ask for a storage mode: Import or Direct Query. Section three explains how to choose. To reuse work that someone else already published, use a shared semantic model. On the Home tab choose Get data, then Power B I semantic models, and pick the model. You build new reports on the existing model instead of copying the data. The measures and relationships stay in one place, so every report shows the same numbers.

1.title: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models, continued
1.text: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models. Same measures and no extra copy of the data. Connect to the shared semantic model. Your own shaping of a source. Connect to the source with a Power Query connector. You need Build permission on the model to create new content from it (module fifteen). A source on a private network or on-premises needs a gateway for refresh in the service (module fourteen). Cloud sources do not. Exam tip: To build a new report on an existing semantic model without copying data, use Get data, then Power B I semantic models. It needs Build permission on the model.

1.title: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels
1.text: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels. In the Power Query Editor choose Data source settings on the Home tab. In Desktop you find it under Transform data on the Home tab. The dialog lists the sources in the current file and the global permissions saved on your computer.

1.title: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels, continued
1.text: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels. Edit Permissions. Change the credentials and the privacy level. Clear Permissions. Remove saved credentials so Power B I asks again. Change Source. Point the query at another server, database or file path. The credential type must match the source, such as Windows, Basic (user name and password), Organizational account or Anonymous. After you publish, the refresh credentials live in the semantic model settings in the service. Only the model owner can edit them. Another user must take over the model first.

1.title: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels, continued
1.text: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels. Privacy levels stop Power Query from sending data from one source to another by accident when it combines sources. Each source has its own level. None. No level is set yet. Private. Sensitive: its data is never sent to any other source. Organizational. Its data can go to Private and Organizational sources, not Public ones. Public. Its data can go to any source.

1.title: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels, continued
1.text: Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels. When a query would break these rules, Power Query blocks the combination and shows an error about privacy levels. The option to ignore privacy levels is off by default and does not apply to published models. Exam tip: Private data is never sent to another source, and Public data can go to any source. Organizational sits between them: it can go to Private and Organizational sources, not Public. Exam tip: Credentials and privacy levels are set in Data source settings, with Edit Permissions. In the service, only the model owner edits the credentials.

1.title: Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import
1.text: Choose between Direct Lake, Direct Query and Import. The storage mode decides where the data lives and when it is current. Import and Direct Query work with any license. Data. Import: Copied into the in-memory model. Direct Query: Stays in the source. Direct Lake: Delta tables in One Lake, read by the Verti Paq engine. Current when. Import: After a refresh. Direct Query: Every visual queries the source. Direct Lake: A refresh copies only metadata (framing), in seconds. Refresh. Import: Pro: up to eight a day; P P U, Premium, Fabric: up to forty-eight. Direct Query: Dashboard tiles refresh hourly by default. Direct Lake: No gateway can refresh it.

1.title: Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import, continued
1.text: Choose between Direct Lake, Direct Query and Import. Limits. Import: Data must fit the model. Direct Query: A query over one million rows fails; service timeout four minutes; ten connections per source by default. Direct Lake: Needs a Fabric capacity (F skew); not in My workspace. Also. Import: Fully interactive visuals. Direct Query: Needs query folding; no automatic date hierarchy, so build a date table. Direct Lake: No hybrid tables, partitions or user-defined aggregations.

1.title: Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import, continued
1.text: Choose between Direct Lake, Direct Query and Import. Choose Direct Query when the data changes too often, is too large to import, the source security must be kept (single sign-on), data-sovereignty rules limit copies, or the source has server-defined measures. Choose Direct Lake when the data is already Delta tables in One Lake and you want Import-like speed without scheduled copies. Choose Import when none of those apply. Direct Lake on One Lake does not fall back to Direct Query. Direct Lake on sequel endpoints can fall back to Direct Query, for example for sequel views, granular sequel security or when guardrails are exceeded. The model property is Direct Lake behavior.

1.title: Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import, continued
1.text: Choose between Direct Lake, Direct Query and Import. Other options mix modes. Hybrid tables combine Import and Direct Query partitions. Dual storage suits shared dimensions. Aggregation tables and automatic aggregations speed up Direct Query. Exam tip: Import: Pro allows up to eight scheduled refreshes a day, and P P U, Premium and Fabric allow up to forty-eight. Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata. Exam tip: Direct Query: a query returning more than one million rows fails, the service timeout is four minutes and the default is ten connections per source. Direct Lake needs a Fabric capacity, and no gateway can refresh it.

2.title: Create and modify parameters
2.text: Create and modify parameters. A parameter stores a value that queries can use, so you change the value once instead of editing many queries. Create one on the Home tab with Manage Parameters, then New Parameter. You can also right-click a query that holds a constant and choose Convert to Parameter.

2.title: Create and modify parameters, continued
2.text: Create and modify parameters. Name. How steps refer to the parameter. Description. Help text for the person who changes it. Required. Whether a value must be given. Type. Any, Text, Decimal Number, Date and so on. Suggested Values. Any value, List of values or Query. Default Value. The value used when none is chosen. Current Value. The value the queries use now.

2.title: Create and modify parameters, continued
2.text: Create and modify parameters. A parameter does nothing until a step uses it. Edit the step, for example Filter Rows or the Source step, and pick the parameter instead of a typed value. On the View tab choose Parameters, then Always allow, so that the dialogs offer your parameters. Parameters let you switch the source, server, database, file path or filter values. They also drive Direct Query dynamic M parameters. To modify a parameter, open Manage Parameters and edit its properties or its current value. After publishing, the model owner can change values in the semantic model settings in the service.

2.title: Create and modify parameters, continued
2.text: Create and modify parameters. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Switch between a test and a production server with a parameter used in the Source step. Convert to Parameter turns a constant query into a parameter.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A finance team published a semantic model with approved measures. An analyst needs a new report that uses the same measures and must not copy the data. What should the analyst do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Use Get data and the Power B I semantic models option. Connecting to the shared semantic model reuses its measures and relationships without a second copy of the data.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An analyst changed a sequel database password, and Power B I Desktop now asks for credentials. Where can the saved credentials be updated? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: In Data source settings, with Edit Permissions. Saved credentials and privacy levels are changed in Data source settings with Edit Permissions.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A query combines a salary table with a public web table. The salary data must never be sent to any other source. Which setting should the salary source have? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Private, so its data goes to no other source. Only the Private level stops a source's data from being sent to any other source.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A retailer keeps sales as Delta tables in One Lake on a Fabric F skew capacity. Analysts want Import-like speed without scheduled copies of the data. Which storage mode fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Direct Lake mode on the One Lake Delta tables. Direct Lake reads the Delta tables in One Lake with the Verti Paq engine, so nothing is copied on a schedule.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A team must switch the same report between a test server and a production server without editing each query. What should the analyst create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A parameter for the server, used in the Source step. A parameter used in the Source step lets you change the server in one place.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A large model moves from Import to Direct Lake. What does a refresh of the Direct Lake model now do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: It copies only metadata, which takes seconds. A Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata (framing), so it completes in seconds.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the four privacy levels? Answer: None, Private, Organizational and Public. Question two. What happens to a Direct Query query that returns more than one million rows? Answer: It fails. Question three. Where do you edit saved credentials in Desktop? Answer: Data source settings, with Edit Permissions.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many scheduled refreshes a day does Pro allow, and how many do P P U, Premium and Fabric allow? Answer: Up to eight on Pro, and up to forty-eight on P P U, Premium and Fabric. Question five. What does Direct Lake read? Answer: Delta tables in One Lake, on a Fabric capacity. Question six. How do you create a parameter? Answer: Home, then Manage Parameters, then New Parameter, or Convert to Parameter on a constant query.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Shared model: Get data, Power B I semantic models: reuse measures, no copy; needs Build permission. Data source settings: Edit Permissions (credentials, privacy level), Clear Permissions, Change Source. Privacy levels: None; Private never sent; Organizational not to Public; Public to any source. Import: data copied into the model. Direct Query: data stays in the source; over one million rows fails; four-minute timeout. Direct Lake: Delta tables in One Lake; Fabric F skew; no gateway; refresh copies metadata. Parameters: Manage Parameters or Convert to Parameter; Type, Suggested Values, Current Value.
